title: Multimodal Remote Inference
abstract: arXiv:2508.07555v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We consider a remote inference system with multiple modalities, where a multimodal machine learning (ML) model performs real-time inference using features collected from remote sensors. When sensor observations evolve dynamically over time, fresh features are critical for inference tasks. However, timely delivery of features from all modalities is often infeasible under limited network resources. To address this challenge, we formulate a multimodal scheduling problem to minimize the ML model's inference error. We model this error as a general function of the Age of Information (AoI) vector, where AoI quantifies data freshness. We cast the problem as a semi-Markov decision process (SMDP) and derive an equivalent reformulation with a reduced state set. tldr: 该论文针对多模态远程推理系统提出了一种以最小化机器学习推理误差为目标的多模态调度问题，将推理误差建模为信息年龄向量的函数，通过半马尔可夫决策过程求解，并揭示了双模态与多模态情形下最优策略链结构的本质差异。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates a multimodal scheduling problem for remote inference systems to minimize ML inference error, models the error as a general function of the Age of Information vector, solves it via a semi-Markov decision process with a reduced state set, and reveals fundamentally different chain structures of optimal policies between the two-modality and multi-modality cases.
